arxiv-2102-07109.title: Machine Learning Methods for the Design and Operation of Liquid Rocket Engines – Research Activities at the DLR Institute of Space Propulsion
arxiv-2102-07109.creator: Günther Waxenegger-Wilfing , Kai Dresia, Jan Deeken and Michael Oschwald
arxiv-2102-07109.description: Abstract The last years have witnessed an enormous interest in the use of artificial intelligence methods, especially machine learning algorithms. This also has a major impact on aerospace engineering in general, and the design and operation of liquid rocket engines in particular, and research in this area is growing rapidly.

arxiv-2107-08707.title: A Measure Theoretical Approach to the Mean-field Maximum Principle for Training NeurODEs
arxiv-2107-08707.creator: Benoît Bonnet, Cristina Cipriani, Massimo Fornasier, Hui Huang
arxiv-2107-08707.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Benoît Bonnet, Cristina Cipriani, Massimo Fornasier, Hui Huang. In this paper we consider a measure-theoretical formulation of the training of NeurODEs in the form of a mean-field optimal control with L 2 L^{2} -regularization of the control. We derive first order optimality conditions for the NeurODE training problem in the form of a mean-field maximum principle, and show that it admits a unique control solution, which is Lipschitz continuous in time.

arxiv-2203-17047.title: Ab initio machine learning of phase space averages
arxiv-2203-17047.creator: Jan Weinreich, Dominik Lemm, Guido Falk von Rudorff, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld
arxiv-2203-17047.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jan Weinreich, Dominik Lemm, Guido Falk von Rudorff, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld. Equilibrium structures determine material properties and biochemical functions. We propose to machine learn phase-space averages, conventionally obtained by ab initio or force-field based molecular dynamics (MD) or Monte Carlo simulations. In analogy to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), our ab initio machine learning (AIML) model does not require bond topologies and therefore enables a general machine learning pathway to ensemble properties throughout chemical compound space.

arxiv-2208-05890.title: Speech Synthesis with Mixed Emotions Thanks: Kun Zhou is with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, National University of Singapore, Singapore. E-mail: zhoukun@u.nus.edu Berrak Sisman is with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Texas at Dallas
arxiv-2208-05890.creator: Kun Zhou, Berrak Sisman, Rajib Rana
arxiv-2208-05890.description: Abstract Emotional speech synthesis aims to synthesize human voices with various emotional effects. The current studies are mostly focused on imitating an averaged style belonging to a specific emotion type. In this paper, we seek to generate speech with a mixture of emotions at run-time.

arxiv-2306-13195.title: Prompt to GPT-3: Step-by-Step Thinking Instructions for Humor Generation
arxiv-2306-13195.creator: Yuetian Chen, Bowen Shi, Mei Si
arxiv-2306-13195.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence has made significant progress in natural language processing, with models like GPT-3 demonstrating impressive capabilities. However, these models still have limitations when it comes to complex tasks that require an understanding of the user, such as mastering human comedy writing strategies.

arxiv-2309-11110.title: Variational Structures for Infinite Transition Orbits of Monotone Twist Maps
arxiv-2309-11110.creator: Yuika Kajihara
arxiv-2309-11110.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider chaotic dynamics and variational structures of area-preserving maps. There is a lot of study on the dynamics of their maps and the works of Poincare and Birkhoff are well-known. To consider variational structures of area-preserving maps, we define a special class of area-preserving maps called monotone twist maps .

arxiv-2312-03838.title: Hayden-Preskill recovery in chaotic and integrable unitary circuit dynamics
arxiv-2312-03838.creator: Michael A. Rampp, Pieter W. Claeys
arxiv-2312-03838.description: Abstract The Hayden-Preskill protocol probes the capability of information recovery from local subsystems after unitary dynamics. As such it resolves the capability of quantum many-body systems to dynamically implement a quantum error-correcting code. The transition to coding behavior has been mostly discussed using effective approaches, such as entanglement membrane theory.

arxiv-2408-09870.title: 1d Conformal Field Theory and Dispersion Relations
arxiv-2408-09870.creator: Dean Carmi, Sudip Ghosh, Trakshu Sharma
arxiv-2408-09870.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dean Carmi, Sudip Ghosh, Trakshu Sharma. We study conformal field theory in d = 1 d=1 space-time dimensions. We derive a dispersion relation for the 4-point correlation function of identical bosons and fermions, in terms of the double discontinuity. This extends the conformal dispersion relation of [ 1 ] , which holds for CFTs in dimensions d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 , to the case of d = 1 d=1 .

arxiv-2410-01367.title: Towards Dynamic Graph Neural Networks with Provably High-Order Expressive Power
arxiv-2410-01367.creator: Zhe Wang, Tianjian Zhao, Zhen Zhang, Jiawei Chen, Sheng Zhou, Yan Feng, Chun Chen, Can Wang
arxiv-2410-01367.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhe Wang, Tianjian Zhao, Zhen Zhang, Jiawei Chen, Sheng Zhou, Yan Feng, Chun Chen, Can Wang. Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DyGNNs) have garnered increasing research attention for learning representations on evolving graphs. Despite their effectiveness, the limited expressive power of existing DyGNNs hinders them from capturing important evolving patterns of dynamic graphs. Although some works attempt to enhance expressive capability with heuristic features, there remains a lack of DyGNN frameworks with provable and quantifiable high-order expressive power.

arxiv-2504-15463.title: Double-pass rotating z-cut quartz plate as a rapidly variable waveplate
arxiv-2504-15463.creator: Byungjin Lee, 1 Kiryang Kwon, 1 and Jae-yoon Choi 1, † \dagger
arxiv-2504-15463.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Byungjin Lee, 1 Kiryang Kwon, 1 and Jae-yoon Choi 1, † \dagger. We demonstrate a rapidly tunable waveplate based on a rotating z-cut quartz plate in a double-pass configuration. In contrast to previous single-pass implementations, where angular rotation of birefringent crystals causes significant beam path displacement, we show that the double-pass geometry effectively suppresses beam walk-off, reducing lateral shifts to below 10 μ \mu{} m, which is stable enough to have a fiber coupling.

pmc-10698791.creator: Magdalena Romanowicz, Kyle S Croarkin, Rana Elmaghraby, Michelle Skime, Paul E Croarkin, Jennifer L Vande Voort, Julia Shekunov, Arjun P Athreya
pmc-10698791.description: Objective:Parents frequently purchase and inquire about smartwatch devices to monitor child behaviors and functioning. The study team completed continuous behavioral phenotyping during study participation.

pmc-11674693.description: Lateral flow assays are widely used in point-of-care diagnostics but face challenges in sensitivity and accuracy when detecting low analyte concentrations, such as thyroid-stimulating hormone biomarkers. This study aims to enhance assay performance by leveraging textural features and hybrid artificial intelligence models.

pmc-12403272.title: Usefulness of biofeedback as a potentially educational treatment of temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-12403272.creator: Ada María González-González, Manuel Tello Pellitero, Natalia López Tejerina, Xabier A Soto-Goñi, Juan Nicolás Cuenca-Zaldívar, Eleuterio A Sánchez-Romero
pmc-12403272.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo evaluate the effectiveness of biofeedback (BF) as a potential educational treatment for temporomandibular disorders (TMD) through a systematic review and a network meta-analysis.MethodsA systematic search was conducted across five electronic databases (PubMed, Web of Science, PEDro, Scopus, and Cochrane Library) to identify clinical trials using BF as a therapeutic intervention in patients diagnosed with TMD according to RDC/TMD or DC/TMD criteria. A frequentist fixed-effects network meta-analysis was performed with robust variance estimation to account for within-study correlations in the repeated measures.

pmc-12469232.title: TP53 IVS3 16 bp Variant and Breast Cancer Risk in Western Mexican Women: A Case–Control Study
pmc-12469232.creator: Mariana Araiza-Guzmán, Bricia M. Gutiérrez-Zepeda, Ana M. Saldaña-Cruz, Ingrid B. Montoya-Delgado, Diana Rubio-Delgado, Pablo Benítez-Villa, Diana M. Hernández-Corona, Adrian Daneri-Navarro, Alicia del Toro-Arreola, Jazmin Márquez-Pedroza, Antonio Quintero-Ramos, Betsabé Contreras-Haro
pmc-12469232.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Mutations in the TP53 gene can alter its tumor suppressor functions, thereby promoting oncogenic activity. The TP53 IVS3 16 bp genetic variant overlaps with nucleotide sequences that can alter regulatory structures, potentially affecting its function. The aim of the present study was to evaluate the association between TP53 IVS3 16 bp genetic variant and the risk of breast cancer (BC) in women from western Mexico. Methods: The study included 220 women diagnosed with BC and 198 cancer-free controls.

pmc-12472971.title: Semi-Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Novel Sinomenine Derivatives
pmc-12472971.creator: Meichun Wu, Zhewei Zhang, Ze Li, Zijian Zhao, Jay McLaughlin
pmc-12472971.description: Sinomenine has long been known as an anti-inflammatory drug, while poor efficiency and large-dose treatment had limited its further application. Five novel sinomenine 1-Br-4-cinnamic acid esters derivatives 2a–2e were designed and synthesized to improve its analgesic and anti-inflammatory activity. All synthesized sinomenine derivatives were structurally confirmed by NMR and ESI-MS.

pmc-12502427.title: ACOXL-AS1’s pan-cancer dynamics and its proliferative impact on endometrial endometrioid carcinoma
pmc-12502427.creator: Hongrong Wu, Ruilin Lin, Liangli Hong
pmc-12502427.description: BackgroundLong non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are critically involved in carcinogenesis; however, the pan-cancer significance and functional mechanisms of ACOXL-AS1 remain largely uncharacterized. This study comprehensively investigates the expression landscape, prognostic value, and biological impact of ACOXL-AS1 across multiple malignancies, with a specific focus on its pro-proliferative role in endometrial endometrioid carcinoma (EEC).

pmc-12657363.title: Stability of formoterol concentration in scalp hair of patients using maintenance formoterol therapy for asthma or COPD (INCTFISH)
pmc-12657363.creator: E. Sportel, K. Wagelaar, M. Brusse-Keizer, J. van der Palen, H. van Veen, M. Wessels, J. van Boven, D. Touw, K. Movig
pmc-12657363.description: IntroductionHair testing provides a non-invasive, objective method with a long (retrospective) surveillance window for assessing medication adherence. Previous studies have developed a method to analyze formoterol in hair and suggest a possible dose-response relationship. The INCTFISH study aims to assess the stability of formoterol concentrations in hair in patients using formoterol for asthma or COPD maintenance therapy.

pmc-12698959.title: Prophylactic Management of Vestibular Migraine: A Systematic Review
pmc-12698959.creator: Hussain Ali Almohammed, Husna Irfan Thalib, Kawthar Faisal Kushara, Bushra Wadi Bin Saddiq, Bayan Mohammed Khair Al Zoabi, Tanveer Nidal Khan, Ahmed Salah Morad, Rimas Warid Aljuaid, Lamyaa Mohammed Gharawi, Shahad Jawdat Alsaygh, Mable Pereira, Shaima Abuhulayqah
pmc-12698959.description: BackgroundVestibular migraine (VM) is a neurological disorder characterized by episodic vertigo in patients with migraine, contributing to substantial functional impairment. Although VM is relatively common, a consensus on effective prophylactic treatments is lacking. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of pharmacological and adjunct non‐pharmacological interventions for VM management.

pmc-12838582.creator: Nuriza Ulul Azmi, Rezi Riadhi Syahdi, Meidi Utami Puteri, Arry Yanuar, Mitsuyasu Kato, Fadlina Chany Saputri
pmc-12838582.description: Cancer remains a major global health challenge, largely due to its biological heterogeneity and the capacity of tumor cells to adapt under metabolic and environmental stress. Structural equation modeling and bootstrap analysis were employed to test the sequential mediation model.
